title: Article: Why Shiv Tattva Is So Important in Spiritual Practice

segments.text: Shiv Tattva is the energy that makes a person capable of receiving and holding divine (cosmic) energy. Our ancient saints have always emphasized — without worshipping Lord Shiva, no sadhana (spiritual practice) can truly succeed.

That’s because Lord Shiva blesses the seeker with Shiv Tattva — a kind of inner container or vessel. Imagine Bhagwan Ram’s energy as a sacred liquid. Without a proper vessel, that energy will simply spill or be lost. Shiv Tattva is the vessel that holds, absorbs, and awakens this energy within you.

This is why Bhagwan Shiv is called Mahadev — the Great God. Every deity carries a spark of Shiv Tattva within them. But Lord Shiva is unique — he doesn’t carry the energy (tattva) of any other deity. He is the original source.

In the spiritual path of Ashaeiynn, once a seeker completes their aura shielding through the initiated mantra, only then are they given Shiv Tattva — not just through words, but with the support of Ashaeiynn’s divine energies (Dev Shaktis).

After receiving Shiv Tattva, Bhagwan Ram’s energy is gradually awakened inside the body. This becomes the starting point for deeper transformation — including the awakening of the Kundalini Shakti and the third eye.
A Simple Example: The Cup and the Water

Think of Lord Ram’s divine energy as pure water, and Shiv Tattva as the cup. Without the cup, how will you hold or drink the water? Even if you have access to the purest water, you won’t benefit from it unless you have something to hold it in.

In the same way, no matter how powerful the mantra or the energy, without Shiv Tattva — the inner vessel — it cannot settle or activate within you. Once you have Shiv Tattva, your spiritual journey truly begins.

This is why Aghori sadhus are considered the purest devotees of Mahadev. They carry only Shiv Tattva within them — not the tattva of any other deity. Because of this, they don’t attract material blessings like wealth, comfort, or luxury that often come from other deities.
But what they lack in worldly possessions, they gain in spiritual power.
With Shiv Tattva alone, they hold immense inner strength and the ability to do wonders that go beyond what the material world can offer.
Want Power? You Need Shiv Tattva — But There’s a Catch.
To gain real spiritual power — and even worldly success — a person must have Shiv Tattva. It’s the divine energy that makes mantras work, awakens Kundalini, and fuels transformation.
But here’s the catch:
Shiv Tattva always comes with a dosh — a spiritual burden that holds you back from fully enjoying worldly power.
That’s why many powerful sadhaks can help others, but feel stuck in their own life.
So How Can You Have Both Power & Prosperity?
If someone wants both — Shakti (spiritual energy) and success in the physical world — they must work to remove the dosh.
But no deity removes this dosh for you.
It can only be cleared through:
Guru Tattva (divine guidance)
Tarak Mantra rituals
Energized mantras practiced with sincerity
Deities may help you manage the dosh, but the real work is yours.
The Truth About Bhog & Blessings
Most people think they’re offering food (bhog) to deities. But in many cases, negative entities hijack the offering — and that’s why prayers don’t seem to work.
This happens especially when a person’s third eye isn’t awakened. Without it, we can’t see who’s really receiving the offering.
Final Takeaway
Everyone has some kind of dosh.
Deities help you survive with it — but only you can remove it.
With Shiv Tattva + proper sadhana, you can change your destiny.
Note:
Sometimes, when we pray for one specific thing — like a job, relationship, or healing — and also hope to receive other blessings, nothing seems to work.
In such cases, we must understand: we are carrying a dosh. And because of that dosh, even the deities can’t help us fully.
It’s not that the gods don’t care — they do. But the dosh acts like a barrier. So instead of getting upset or speaking negatively about the deities, we need to realize:
They aren’t ignoring us… they’re simply bound by the rules of cosmic law.
And it’s up to us — with the guidance of Guru Tattva and the right sadhana — to clear that dosh ourselves.
Shiv Tattva is the spark. The rest is your journey.
